verdict.rationale: Daytona's docs state that you define the base OS, runtimes, packages and setup in an image or Dockerfile, and Daytona builds it into a snapshot that serves as a reusable sandbox template. Snapshots can be managed via the CLI and backed by warm pools. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of custom image builds, and explicit documentation of pulling pre-built images from private registries.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define custom sandbox templates or bring my own container image

citations.quote: define the base operating system, language runtimes, packages, and project-level setup in an image or Dockerfile, and Daytona builds it into a snapshot you can use to create sandboxes
Snapshots are persistent, point-in-time captures of sandbox state, including the filesystem, installed packages, dependencies, and settings.
including managing their lifecycle, snapshots, and more
